notes.fact: Zelensky says Russian bombs hit a school used as shelter and aid hub in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region; at least 33 confirmed dead and about 50 unaccounted for.
Russia's defence ministry says it targeted Ukrainian military units near Komyshuvakha and two other settlements, killing up to 25 servicemen; it did not address civilian deaths in the quoted report.
Zelensky says Russia fired 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles overnight at power plants and substations from Odesa to Rivne.
notes.event: Nov 3 strike on Ukraine's energy grid

notes.fact: Russia's defence ministry says it struck power facilities supplying military factories and the Ukrainian army, naming four thermal plants and substations in Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions.
notes.event: Nov 3 strike on Ukraine's energy grid

notes.fact: Ukraine hit a Samara oil refinery, ending a two-week pause on striking Russian energy; Russian strikes on Dnipro cut power for over 350,000 people.
Russian officials say a Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl overnight; Zelensky also reported a strike on a missile-related factory in Rostov region.
Witkoff says the US will mediate Russia-Ukraine working-level talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11 on security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian steps.
Analysts quoted by RFE/RL doubt a breakthrough, citing deep gaps over a ceasefire and security guarantees; the Kremlin says the Oleshky truce does not mean readiness for a wider one.
This is the fourth US-brokered trilateral round since January; the previous three ended without a comprehensive deal, and talks stalled after the US-Iran war began in late February.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov says European officials taking part in the trilateral talks would be impossible, while Europeans fear being cut out of any deal.
German Chancellor Merz, beside Zelensky in Berlin, said he sees no sign Russia is serious about a ceasefire; both want Europe to shape any peace.
Russia's human rights commissioner told CNN she worked with the US first lady's team to secure the Oleshky convoy agreement.
i24NEWS reports NATO is boosting weapons support for Kyiv and that the US approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine.
Three maritime drones struck the Liberian-flagged container ship Contship Jet off Bulgaria, per Bulgaria's defence minister; the crew of 18 was rescued and taken to Varna.
notes.key: claim:bulgarian defence minister not a party

notes.fact: The ship, chartered by Israel's Zim, sank about 12 hours after the attack with 421 containers; Zim said the expected financial damage was minimal.
Bulgaria's outgoing defence chief says the attacking drones came from the east; Sofia shared data with allies. Israel Hayom notes the craft looked like a new type.
notes.key: claim:bulgarian defence chief not a party

notes.fact: Euronews says Russia is suspected in the wave of ship attacks but responsibility for Contship Jet is unproven; it was the fifth drone incident in Bulgaria's waters in October.
A Substack analysis says the drone resembled a Russian design but designs can be copied, and no conclusive public evidence names Ukraine or Russia; treat as commentary.
After seven strikes on ships near Romania and Bulgaria in October, NATO said it would add maritime patrol aircraft, radars and drones in the Black Sea.
notes.event: NATO response to Black Sea strikes

notes.fact: CNN reports drones struck at least a dozen merchant ships in recent weeks, killing more mariners than the Iran war; Ukraine's September wheat exports were 1.09 million tons, half of a year earlier.
Tusk says border guards saw people with flashlights near Sępopol just after midnight; RMF24 reports no one crossed and they withdrew into Kaliningrad.
Tusk acknowledged officials cannot say for certain this was a provocation; the people's identities and intentions are not established.
Tusk says allied warnings, including from NATO's SACEUR, pointed to possible sabotage or armed incursions in the first half of November; Poland added police and counterterrorism units.
Tusk's opponents accused him of using the border alert to distract from a Constitutional Tribunal dispute, the NYT reported; he denies this and urged critics not to serve Russian interests.
Polish police said a readiness order for officers from Nov 2 to 8 was prompted by sabotage threats, not the political dispute; no end date for the deployment is given.
Russia sent NATO a diplomatic note saying it would use its full arsenal, including nuclear weapons, if NATO tried to isolate Kaliningrad; Russia's own claim of a planned blockade.
NATO replied that it is defensive and none of its activities threaten Russia; Rutte told Moscow to stop nuclear threats, and a Kremlin spokesman called the warnings reminders to 'hotheads'.
Moldova's president says a Russian Geran drone crashed near homes and an energy facility; police found it under 100 metres from a house, with no casualties, and a Russian diplomat was expelled.
notes.key: claim:moldovan president not a warring party

notes.fact: Russia's foreign ministry called the expulsion hostile, promised a firm response, and said no evidence of the drone's origin had been shown.
Moldova planned border-crossing shelters on Oct 7, after a projectile ricocheted into a bus and booth at Palanca on Oct 5, lightly injuring a border guard.
NBC's war page carries a headline that fake nuclear-danger alerts appeared as Ukraine and Russia reported hacks of emergency apps; I found no details, actor or advisory.
US officials told Times of Israel the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday; they called it limited, defensive and not a return to major combat.
CBS cites US military officials saying Revolutionary Guards fired at a US fighter jet, which returned fire; Iran later fired a missile from Qeshm that threatened shipping.
Iranian state outlet IRNA reported five rapid explosions on Qeshm and residents saw two aircraft; the Wall Street Journal called it one of several quiet US strikes in recent weeks.
notes.key: claim:iranian state media irna and unnamed us officials
notes.claim_by: party:Iranian state media IRNA and unnamed US officials

notes.fact: Stars and Stripes says the US sought to keep the recent smaller strikes quiet so as not to signal that major combat is resuming, per CNN and WSJ reporting.
Iran's security council secretary Rezaei called the US reply unconvincing and said Hormuz reopens only if Iran's seven conditions are met.
UKMTO said two vessels reported attacks while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, according to ABC's live blog. A separate UKMTO report on Nov. 2 had a ship struck off Oman.
Times of Israel relays a NYT report that some US officials think the intelligence pushing Trump toward renewed war is weak, and Gulf states call it unserious.
Trump said the US could strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site within an hour, and called the conflict a very soft war, per Fox and ABC live blogs.
Four military sources told Reuters the Houthis reached within 80 km of Aden, their closest since 2015, after taking Al-Maqatirah district over about three days.
Dawn reports Houthis advanced within 80 km of Aden while trading cross-border strikes with the Saudi-led coalition on Monday, per military sources and officials.
Yemeni government-run Saba said a missile hit a health centre in Lahj, killing or injuring at least 20 civilians; no breakdown or attribution was given.
JPost, citing Al-Ain, says the Houthis have for weeks hit Saudi airports, energy sites and cities with drones and missiles; the war escalated again in July.
AFP reports Israeli strikes killed at least eight people in Gaza on Sunday, per hospital officials and Hamas's interior ministry; Israel said it targeted militants.
notes.key: claim:gaza health and interior ministries israeli military
notes.claim_by: party:Gaza health and interior ministries; Israeli military

notes.fact: Anadolu, via Middle East Monitor, reports three Palestinians killed on Tuesday, including a security officer and a girl; Gaza's ministry now counts 1,599 killed since the truce.

L'Orient Today (AFP photo) says negotiators have not agreed terms for Hamas to disarm or Israel to withdraw; Israeli troops hold about two-thirds of Gaza, and Israel says four soldiers died since the truce.
Kan, via AJN, says Israel asked Lebanon through US mediators to set up army checkpoints so Hezbollah cannot join a renewed Iran war.
UN News says OCHA recorded at least 160 settler attacks linked to the olive harvest in the first two weeks of October, sometimes with Israeli forces' protection or participation.
The Washington Post says dozens of masked settlers attacked villagers at Abu Falah and beat photojournalist Heidi Levine; witnesses said soldiers did not intervene.
A Palestinian government commission says 1,369 settler attacks were recorded in October, up from 647 in September. This is a Palestinian-side tally, not independently verified.
notes.key: claim:palestinian wall and settlement resistance commission
notes.claim_by: party:Palestinian Wall and Settlement Resistance Commission

notes.fact: Haaretz cites Palestinian reports that settlers kept attacking harvesters on Saturday, with olive oil output estimated to be halved by the attacks.
A Middle East Monitor headline says thousands were displaced as the Israeli army continued an offensive in Hebron; no further detail was in the snippet.
Iraqi security officials said at least two drones were intercepted near Baghdad's Green Zone on Oct. 27; embassy air defences activated, and no damage or casualties were reported.
Wikipedia's Iraq article says US and Saudi forces struck Popular Mobilization Forces sites on 29 July after over 30 drone attacks on Saudi oil sites and US forces. Unverified summary source.

Syria's Health Ministry says the Jordanian strikes killed seven civilians, including three children; Damascus denies prior coordination and closed the Nassib crossing, which reopened a day later, per FDD.
Jordan and Syria agreed to form a joint security committee to investigate the strikes and share intelligence, per VOA, a sign that tensions are being contained.
Jordan's armed forces say border guards stopped 14 armed people entering from Syria on Friday; some fled back. Their identity is not given.
A suspected RSF drone killed at least seven people and injured 36 at a South Kordofan fuel station on 3 November, local sources told the outlet.
notes.event: Drone strike on El Abbasiya fuel station

notes.fact: A US newsletter says the attack was probably carried out by the RSF and notes RSF drone activity in South Kordofan has apparently risen recently.
notes.event: Drone strike on El Abbasiya fuel station

notes.fact: Sudan's army says its air defences downed a Chinese-made FH-95 drone south of Wad Banda on Monday evening and did not say who flew it.
notes.event: Army downs drone in West Kordofan

notes.fact: North Kordofan's government accused the RSF of drone attacks on service facilities and fuel stations in Al-Rahad and Umm Rawaba on 22–23 October, citing no casualty figures.
notes.event: RSF drone attacks in North Kordofan

notes.fact: UN envoy Pekka Haavisto told The National the UN plans talks with the RSF-allied bloc before Christmas on a transition to civilian rule.
notes.event: UN envoy plans talks with RSF bloc

notes.fact: A Brazilian outlet reports no date or venue is set for the UN meeting with the RSF-allied bloc; Addis Ababa is only a possible venue.
notes.event: UN envoy plans talks with RSF bloc

notes.fact: Army chief Burhan rejected negotiations on 6 October and vowed to retake all RSF-held territory, according to an African defence outlet.
UN Secretary-General Guterres condemned recent drone strikes hitting water treatment sites, humanitarian trucks and hospitals; Haavisto said attacks intensified in Abyei, Kordofan and Darfur.
notes.event: UN condemns drone attacks on civilian sites

notes.fact: Ethiopia told the UN Security Council on 9 October that Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 km into Tigray; Eritrea denies this and Al Jazeera says it is unverified.
A US outlet reports Ethiopia cited UN Charter Article 51 on self-defence in its letter and says Ethiopia will defend itself against the incursion.
Ethiopia expelled all Eritrean diplomats on 1 October, citing hostility, and diplomatic ties between the two states have since been severed.
An analysis says the US State Department warned on 3 October that war would put US cooperation at risk, and fighting remains in Tigray, far from the coast.
AFRICOM says it struck al-Shabaab on 17, 19 and 21 October, in coordination with Somalia's government; the 17 October strike was near Dhooble Airport.
A Nigerian outlet says AFRICOM's published register showed 88 strikes in Somalia in 2026 at the time of writing, against al-Shabaab and ISIS-Somalia.
Critical Threats' 29 October Africa File lists an al-Shabaab ambush in South West State; the snippet gave no casualty details.
notes.event: Al-Shabaab ambush in South West State

notes.fact: Critical Threats says former president Joseph Kabila officially joined the M23 rebellion as political leader of a rebranded movement called the FRN.
notes.event: Kabila joins M23 rebranded as FRN

notes.fact: Tuareg rebels announced a deal letting Russian forces backing Mali's army leave Kidal, which they said they fully controlled, after the 25–26 April attacks.
Critical Threats says JNIM and FLA seized Gao, Kidal and Bourem on 25 April; a car bomb killed Defence Minister Camara, per Wikipedia. Mali's junta later denied losing control.
A crowd-edited encyclopedia says over 100 soldiers died and 92 were captured when JNIM attacked a camp at Dioura on 10 September; not independently checked.
Reuters reports an Algerian army convoy reached Arlit, Niger, in Algeria's first foreign troop deployment since 1973; size and timetable undisclosed.
Al Jazeera says Algeria's president ordered troops to Niger at Niamey's request to protect energy interests; a senator said they are not sent to wage war.
The Council on Foreign Relations tracker, citing Africanews, says a fuel convoy escorted by Algerian forces reached Niger, marking the start of the deployment.
Human Rights Watch says JNIM killed at least 27 civilians in two attacks in Burkina Faso's Yatenga province in September; JNIM did not respond in the excerpt.
notes.event: JNIM attacks on civilians in Yatenga

notes.fact: Taiwan's defence ministry counted 49 Chinese military aircraft, six warships and six government vessels in the 24 hours to 6am Nov 3. An analyst called it an unannounced 'quiet exercise'.
EFE says 49 aircraft is Taiwan's highest daily count of 2026. It also says the 2026 total of 2,335 is about 49% below the same period of 2025.
Storm Media notes China has held no named military drill aimed at Taiwan in 2026. The last one ended in December 2025. Taiwan's local elections are on Nov 28.
A tracking site says PLA aircraft inside Taiwan's ADIZ fell 52% from Jan 1 to Aug 9 against 2025, citing ministry data. It says warship numbers fell only 7%.
On Oct 26 Taiwan's defence ministry reported only three PLA aircraft, six warships and nine official ships. A few days earlier it reported no aircraft at all.
Beijing announced another coast guard patrol off Taiwan's east coast on Oct 31. Taiwan says two Chinese vessels took part, and that radio messages to ships overstep Chinese authority.
notes.event: China Coast Guard patrols east of Taiwan

notes.fact: A Ukrainian outlet reports that, as of Nov 1, there is no naval blockade of Taiwan. It says east-coast patrols have grown markedly since June.
notes.event: China Coast Guard patrols east of Taiwan

notes.fact: Taiwan's Mainland Affairs Council said Beijing is likely to take more aggressive steps as Xi consolidates power. It cited military intimidation and election interference.
Manila's military counted 101 Chinese navy and coast guard ships near Philippine-held features in September, against 56 in August.
notes.event: Chinese ship numbers near-double in September

notes.fact: The Philippine Coast Guard says a Chinese vessel fired a water cannon on Oct 8 and delayed a sailor's evacuation from Ayungin by nearly ten hours. The sailor was stable.
An op-ed reports that a Chinese coast guard ship rammed the Philippine vessel Datu Magat Salamat on Sept 18 while it carried fuel for fishermen.
Manila says a Chinese coast guard crew member hit a Filipino sailor on the head with a baton at Ayungin on July 20. China's embassy says Filipinos provoked it.
The Philippine Coast Guard says Chinese ships used water cannon at Scarborough Shoal on July 23. China's coast guard says it drove away intruding Philippine vessels.
notes.key: claim:philippine coast guard and china coast guard
notes.claim_by: party:Philippine Coast Guard and China Coast Guard

notes.fact: NPR reports China has pressed Japan since Takaichi's Taiwan remarks last year, and that Russia has joined in. The report adds Japan faces a diplomatic dilemma ahead of a possible summit.
Reporting this week says Beijing has cut rare-earth exports to Japan, urged tourists to avoid it, and increased military patrols near Japan. A TV-drama row is the latest friction.
An Asia Times analyst expects relations to worsen as Beijing continues its campaign to isolate Tokyo over Takaichi's Taiwan comment. This is an opinion piece.
A Brookings piece says China tightened dual-use export curbs and listed 20 Japanese firms and universities. Takaichi's party won a record result in a February snap election.
Wikipedia's summary says China refuses dialogue unless Takaichi retracts her remarks, and did not answer Japanese efforts to arrange a leaders' meeting at APEC. Secondary source.
South Korea's military says North Korea fired about a dozen short-range ballistic missiles from Wonsan on Oct 29. Tokyo confirmed a launch, and the missiles fell outside Japan's economic zone.
notes.claim_by: party:South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff

notes.fact: NBC says the previous launch was Oct 12, during border tension over a mine blast that wounded South Korean soldiers in September. The North has tested missiles more than ten times this year.
notes.claim_by: party:South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff

notes.fact: South Korea's military says North Korea fired an unidentified projectile toward the East Sea on Nov 4. This came less than a week after Seoul proposed military talks on the border.
notes.claim_by: party:South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff

notes.fact: Yonhap says the Nov 4 launch came from the Sondok area in South Hamgyong Province. Seoul and Washington were still analysing it. A cluster-bomb test was reported by North Korean state media on Oct 31.
notes.claim_by: party:South Korean Joint Chiefs of Staff

notes.fact: Long War Journal counts at least three Taliban-Pakistan clashes since Oct 19. Pakistan called the Taliban account lies and said Taliban forces fired first.
Pakistan's information ministry says Afghan firing at Angoor Adda killed one local and hurt five relatives. It says earlier talks, including China-mediated ones, produced no breakthrough.
notes.event: Angoor Adda firing and failed talks

notes.fact: An Afghan outlet reports a clash near Torkham over a border outpost, still ongoing when it published. Officials on neither side had commented.
Pakistan and the Taliban traded fire for about four hours on Oct 17. Afghan media said seven Pakistani soldiers died; Pakistan-linked media said 13 TTP fighters were killed.
notes.key: claim:afghan media and pakistan linked media claims differ
notes.claim_by: party:Afghan media and Pakistan-linked media (claims differ)

notes.fact: Fighting around Paktia and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa since Oct 5 followed Moscow-format talks that ended without a joint statement. Pakistan's ISPR says it killed 12 militants in Kurram.
Pakistan's military media wing says 17 militants and one soldier died in two operations in Kachhi and Kharan on Nov 1. Dawn relays the claim; it is not independently confirmed.
ISPR says an army major died to a roadside bomb in Pasni on Oct 18. It also reported 14 militants killed in several districts on Oct 18.
The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies counted 225 attacks nationwide in September, up 13.1% on August. Balochistan had 131 of them.
notes.key: claim:pakistan institute for conflict and security studies
notes.claim_by: org:Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies

notes.fact: Dawn cites PICSS: Balochistan deaths rose from 109 in June to 372 in July, including 62 security personnel against six in June.
notes.key: claim:pakistan institute for conflict and security studies
notes.claim_by: org:Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies

notes.fact: Dawn reports two people killed and one abducted by armed men in Qila Abdullah on Nov 1 after residents exchanged fire. Officials gave no claimed group.
Haiti's prime minister spoke publicly for the first time since four Salvadoran aviation technicians went missing last month. El Salvador then sent over 2,000 troops.
Per CFR's tracker, which cites the NYT, gangs ambushed a five-soldier Salvadoran patrol in Port-au-Prince and the patrol was reported missing.
Citing the UN human rights office (OHCHR), the Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect says over 8,200 people were killed in Haiti from January 2025 to March 2026.
notes.outlet: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

notes.fact: AP reported that a gang attack on Kenscoff killed 47 people and kidnapped over 50. Police said a gang leader was threatening to attack Tabarre, where the US embassy is located.

Rio Times, citing EFE and Infobae, reports the first airstrike under new president De la Espriella hit the ELN in Catatumbo. The defence ministry says two presumed rebels died and three civilians were hurt.
Colombia relaunched its 'Esparta' campaign in Catatumbo after an attack blamed on the ELN on a military base in Ocaña. Two soldiers died and five were hurt, per the defence ministry.
Voz.us, citing the NYT, says a joint Venezuelan and US-intelligence drone strike in Apure state hit an ELN hub. It reports more than 20 casualties; the date is not given.
The NYT reports that the US military and other American agencies are carrying out operations in Colombia to halt drug trafficking.
Mexico's security chief Harfuch said a wanted Guasave cartel operator with a $5 million US reward died in a Navy clash in Sinaloa. Two people were killed.
Breitbart Texas reports gunmen fired on a bus of junior-high students in Escuinapa, Sinaloa. The driver was hurt and the students were unharmed, per Sinaloa's government.
US Southern Command says a strike on a speedboat in the eastern Pacific killed five people. Al Jazeera says its count of killed since September 2025 is 243.
AP says the strikes have killed at least 240 people in more than 70 strikes, and the administration has offered little evidence its targets were traffickers.
CBS reported the US military says a strike in the Caribbean killed four people on October 4. Its count was at least 235 dead in 70 strikes.

A UN special rapporteur's September report found reasonable grounds to believe the killings amount to crimes against humanity, according to a newstarget.com summary of UPI. Treat this as a secondary source.
CBS reported Hegseth announced the US would extend operations to land. He said Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras agreed to joint operations, and Guatemala denied agreeing. The date is approximate.
notes.event: US land operations in Latin America

notes.fact: Xinhua reports Noboa imposed a midnight-to-5am curfew through 10 November in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas. It is the fourth curfew this year.
Infobae reports police and troops will carry out 'special operations' during the curfew, including raids on properties to detain suspected gang members.
Ecuador's interior ministry says 218 people were arrested on the first curfew night. 155 of the police arrests were for breaking the curfew, and 91 kg of drugs were seized.
Noboa said crime fell 40% during the September curfew. Press accounts differ on whether he meant crime or homicides, and no breakdown was given.
Decree 519 counts 33 night-time homicides, 7% of 483 nationwide, between 17 September and 13 October. That is a small share of killings.

CBS's 60 Minutes reported US-Cuba negotiations stalled earlier this year. A Cuban deputy foreign minister says tougher US measures are hurting Cubans, and Washington says food and medicine are not restricted.
Al Jazeera reports the US sanctioned Cuba's state oil company CUPET. Rubio said sanctions would continue until government change, and Hegseth hinted at military options.
SCMP says the CUPET sanctions came hours after China-Cuba party talks, and Hegseth said at Guantanamo the Pentagon would be postured for any contingency.
APA (Azerbaijan) relays the NYT. A State Department official says no base talks are under way and the idea is far off.
Anadolu (Turkey), via ua.news, says the agreement would cover ship visits, training, exercises and humanitarian aid. Troop numbers and locations would come in later deals.
Al Jazeera says fridges and freezers at over 100 shops in several European countries overheated on Monday Nov 2, after attacks on internet-linked units.
The Hacker News says attackers remotely changed refrigeration control settings at supermarkets in Belgium and elsewhere in Europe. It calls this a new wave that forced stores to pull food.

Cybersecurity Dive says European authorities are probing the grocery refrigerator attacks. It says thousands of refrigerator devices stayed exposed after the earlier French attack, a wider risk for industrial systems.
Defense One, citing two unnamed people, says US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers caused freezer malfunctions at about six military commissaries since late August. The access method is unclear.
notes.event: Freezer attacks at US military bases

notes.fact: CBS News headlines list earlier supermarket refrigeration attacks in France. The overlap with the US base freezer case is in the target type. The shared method has not been confirmed by any outlet.

ABC News reported on Aug 4, citing sources, that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with Iran the prime suspect. Involvement was unconfirmed and supplies saw no widespread disruption.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Iran-linked PLC attacks

notes.fact: TechCrunch reports an updated advisory from the FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA. It says Iranian actors target controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens. Those products are also used in the US.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Iran-linked PLC attacks

notes.fact: NBC News reported on Sept 2, citing four sources, that Iranian hackers also tried to reach US telecom and energy systems. The attempts were reported as unsuccessful so far.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Iran-linked PLC attacks

notes.fact: CSIS's incident list says the IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed the August water campaign across at least a dozen states. It says the US government had not publicly attributed it.
notes.event: CISA advisory on Iran-linked PLC attacks

notes.fact: CISA opened Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month on Nov 2. It urged owners to map dependencies and plan recovery, and said it would stress operational-technology risks.
notes.hotspot: cyber: CISA advisories and exploited flaws
notes.event: CISA safeguards and advisories this week

notes.fact: CISA added WordPress core flaw CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list on Nov 3, with a Nov 6 fix deadline for federal agencies.
notes.hotspot: cyber: CISA advisories and exploited flaws
notes.event: CISA safeguards and advisories this week

notes.fact: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure flaws on Oct 30 after attackers chained them in zero-day attacks. This VPN product is widely used in US organizations.
notes.hotspot: cyber: CISA advisories and exploited flaws
notes.event: CISA safeguards and advisories this week

notes.fact: CISA's homepage lists a Nov 3 ICS advisory for Mitsubishi Electric and Iconics industrial software. It also carries an alert on PHP flaws ('php2shell') allowing remote code execution.
notes.hotspot: cyber: CISA advisories and exploited flaws
notes.event: CISA safeguards and advisories this week

notes.fact: Black Lotus Labs (Lumen) says Chinese group Volt Typhoon used a covert relay network, Silent Train, in four zero-day campaigns against management and edge systems.
notes.hotspot: cyber: China pre-positioning in US networks

notes.fact: Nextgov says Lumen found Silent Train targets mostly US government, defense and university networks, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas. It used TP-Link, Netgear and Fortinet devices also sold in the US.
notes.hotspot: cyber: China pre-positioning in US networks

notes.fact: BleepingComputer says Silent Train sessions are short, with tools wiped afterward, which makes detection hard. Lumen says it was partly a response to the FBI's earlier KV-botnet takedown.
notes.hotspot: cyber: China pre-positioning in US networks

notes.fact: A Bytes Europe analysis says Germany detained two Belarusians suspected of planning arson near a railway and a power line. Romania also probes them over a defence-plant fire.

The same analysis says a third suspect, a Ukrainian citizen, was held in Poland. Romanian prosecutors want all three transferred. It calls Russian direction a possibility that investigators have yet to confirm.

Poland's police chief said counterterrorism police were deployed to the northeast on Nov 2 after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage near Kaliningrad. Officers were on full readiness from Nov 2 to 8.
ACLED analysts say Russia recruits locals via social media for railway arson in Ukraine, over 40 attempts on signalling cabinets. Polish authorities say an FSB-led group prepared train derailments.
notes.event: Russian rail sabotage via recruited proxies

notes.fact: Russia's transport investigators say a court sentenced two men for trying to burn rail relay cabinets, paid via Telegram by a contact abroad. Izvestia reported it Nov 3.
notes.event: Russian rail sabotage via recruited proxies

notes.fact: The UK's NCSC said on Nov 3 that AI-powered malware is highly likely to feature in a ransomware attack on UK critical infrastructure by 2028. It reports no such attack so far.
notes.hotspot: cyber: UK NCSC warning on AI-driven attacks
notes.event: NCSC State of the Cyber Nation

notes.fact: Taipei Times, relaying a Japanese report, says four Chinese survey ships slowed near Taiwan's undersea cable routes. An intelligence firm used AIS data; Chinese intent is unconfirmed.
notes.event: Taiwan survey ships near undersea cables

notes.fact: TechRadar says the EU plans a Greenland-Europe cable, citing worry over the Red Sea route and Baltic anchor-dragging cases. No new cable cut is reported in the last week.
Cloudflare says it blocked 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, up 38%, about 8,226 per hour.
Zelensky said Russia fired 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight, hitting power plants and substations from Odesa in the south to Rivne in the west.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Ukraine's energy grid

notes.fact: DTEK, Ukraine's largest private generator, said three of its five thermal plants went offline; Ukrainian officials reported outages in Kyiv and at least six other regions.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Ukraine's energy grid

notes.fact: Russia's defence ministry says its forces struck electricity facilities in several regions that supply military factories and the Ukrainian army.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Ukraine's energy grid

notes.fact: Zelensky said at least 33 people died when Russia twice bombed a school used for aid distribution in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region; about 50 were believed trapped under rubble.
Russia's defence ministry says it hit power stations in Kyiv and Zhytomyr regions and a cargo vessel near Odesa. A drone attack near Krasnodar reportedly set fire to an Ozon logistics hub.
Kremlin spokesman Peskov confirmed the Russian delegation will be in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11, with Vladimir Medinsky again leading it, as reported by APA's Moscow bureau.
US envoy Witkoff announced US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks for Nov 10-11 in Abu Dhabi. US officials meet European and NATO representatives in Brussels beforehand on security guarantees.

Kyiv Post says no comprehensive deal exists. Security guarantees and Europe's postwar security setup are unresolved, and Russia's deputy foreign minister wants Ukraine to drop NATO ambitions and bar foreign troops.
A six-day local ceasefire around Russian-held Oleshky held through its final day, but NBC says fighting elsewhere and long-range strikes by both sides did not let up.
Romania blamed Russia for a drone strike that sank the Khoryv off its coast, killing one and leaving three missing. Al Jazeera notes Russia has previously denied such attacks.
A commentary piece counts nine vessels struck in October, the last on Oct 28, and says Moscow has not claimed the attacks; no newer sinking appears in it.
Trump confirmed US strikes on an Iranian anti-aircraft facility, calling them a minor attack that was not war; Iranian media said Qeshm Island was hit.
Trump said on Fox he still has to deal with one or two Iranian nuclear sites; ABC reports he floated more action against Pickaxe Mountain while downplaying the war.
Brent fell 7.64% to $104.77 after Trump said Iran wants a deal quickly; Iran says it could reopen Hormuz within two days if its conditions are met.
Reuters, citing sources, says Houthi forces are 80 km from Aden, the closest since 2015, with fighting at a camp at the entrance to Tur al-Bahah district.
UAE outlet Al-Ain reports dozens of government forces and Houthis killed or wounded at Al-Maqatirah, Lahj, as coalition warplanes raided Houthi positions.
A government military official told Xinhua two Houthi ballistic missiles hit a Lahj market, killing one and wounding 10; Houthi-run al-Masirah reported two killed in a Taiz air strike.
notes.claim_by: party:Yemeni government official and Houthi media

notes.fact: The EU condemned Houthi military escalation and attacks on Saudi Arabia, citing the Aden palace strike and the Taiz siege, and demanded all Houthi military action end.
UN investigators warned that RSF drone strikes hit homes, schools, power and water systems in El Obeid, where about 30% of hospitals work, and army-linked forces carry out arbitrary arrests.
notes.key: claim:un independent international fact finding mission for sudan
notes.event: UN fact-finding warning on El Obeid
notes.claim_by: org:UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan

notes.fact: Security Council Report says al-Shabaab has used political disputes to widen its territorial control and keeps staging ambushes and bombings across central and southern Somalia.
notes.key: claim:security council report independent research ngo

notes.fact: AFRICOM's site lists announced airstrikes against al-Shabaab on Oct 19 and Oct 21, 2026, and a strike on Oct 17 near Dhooble; no 30-day gap exists.
Pakistani and Afghan border forces exchanged fire at several points; Torkham closed about five hours over a disputed check post, and one civilian died in mortar fire near Angoor Adda.
notes.event: Torkham and Angoor Adda clashes Nov 1

notes.fact: Taliban-affiliated media said Pakistani shelling in Shkin, Paktika, killed one civilian and wounded two children; Afghan sources called Nov 1 the third Torkham clash in a week.
notes.event: Torkham and Angoor Adda clashes Nov 1

notes.fact: Torkham reopened after border officials agreed through intermediaries to halt construction near the border; tension stayed high in Angoor Adda.
